course_title: Communication & Feeding Difficulties in Children II
course_description: This course introduces students to the planning and implementation of evidence-based interventions for communication and feeding/mealtime management difficulties that can present in children under five years of age. In this course, students undertake practical activities that foster the development and demonstration of critical reflection, clinical reasoning and knowledge of the role of other professions in the holistic management of communication disorders and feeding difficulties in children under five years of age.

course_aims:
This course is a follow-on course from SPCH2111. In this course, students will develop skills in collaborative goal setting and the planning and implementation of evidence-based interventions for communication and/or feeding/mealtime difficulties experienced by children under five years of age. Online self-directed learning activities are supplemented by tutorials in which students will engage in peer-to-peer learning activities to gain experience in critical reflection and clinical reasoning and the ethical provision of person and family-centred services to children under five years of age from diverse backgrounds. Through active engagement in authentic learning opportunities, students will develop an understanding of the role of interprofessional teams in the overall management of communication and feeding/mealtime management difficulties in young children.

This course offers students a flipped approach to learning. Students engage in online learning resources before weekly tutorials where they then participate in authentic learning experiences with peers and teaching staff. In the tutorials, students engage in peer-to-peer learning through active participation in independent, small group and large group inquiry-based learning activities. This provides students with more flexibility to learn, but the associated workload is similar to that of a traditional course.

learning_outcomes.description: Collaborate with families and significant others to develop communication and/or feeding goals for children under five years of age (Speech Pathology Australia Professional Standards, Domains/Standards 1.4, 1.6, 1.7, 2.5, 3.1and 3.4)

Plan and implement an evidence-based intervention for communication and/or feeding difficulties experienced by children under five years of age. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1, 3.4, and 3.5)

Demonstrate critical reflection and clinical reasoning in providing person- and family-centred services to children under five years of age and their significant others. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.4, 1.6, 2.2, 2.5, 3.3, and 3.5)

Describe how to uphold the Code of Ethics when managing children under five years of age with communication and/or feeding difficulties and their families. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, and 1.5).

Develop a culturally responsive intervention plan for children under five years of age who are from an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander background and their families. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 2.1, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1, 3.3 and 3.4)

Describe the role of interprofessional teams in the overall management of communication and feeding difficulties in children under five years of age. (SPA PS Domains/Standards 1.4, 1.7, 2.6, and 3.4).

assessment_details.task_description: This is an authentic assessment that allows you to demonstrate person- and family-centred practice in the context of an intervention session for a young child with communication difficulties. Students will be provided with case information on a young child with fluency difficulties. Individually, each student will complete two components: Session Plan: Each student will write a session plan for the child, targeting relevant intervention goals. Intervention Video : Using clinical reasoning and evidence-based practice, each student will create a video: Summarising the child's intervention plan; and Demonstrating the implementation of an evidence-based intervention approach tailored to the child's needs. assessment_details.title: Holistic management case presentation
assessment_details.category: Paper/ Report/ Annotation, Presentation, Role play/ Simulation
assessment_details.task_description: This is an authentic, group-based assessment that allows you to bring together the theory gained in the course and apply it collaboratively to a case. You will be provided with case information and case data for a young child (0-5 years) presenting with communication and/or swallowing difficulties. Working in a clinical team, you will be required to (a) develop a written intervention plan identifying further assessment, referral, and intervention priorities for this case; and (b) deliver a prerecorded discussion simulating a case conference presentation, in which your team discusses and justifies your clinical decision-making and demonstrates the practical application of selected intervention strategies. Throughout this assessment, you will be expected to draw on evidence-based practice, person- and family-centred care approaches, and alignment with the Professional Standards for Speech Pathologists in Australia (2020) and the Speech Pathology Australia Code of Ethics (2020). Each member of the group will receive the same mark on the completion of the case presentation criteria (15%). Teamwork scores (i.e., Buddycheck) will be based on peer-assessment of group member contributions to the assessment (5%). A detailed task description and marking criteria will be made available on the course Blackboard site. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 12 (27 Jul - 25 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Online self-directed learning modules (self-directed learning) A series of weekly online lectures/modules will provide information on the holistic management of communication and feeding/mealtime difficulties in children under five years of age. The self-directed learning content will cover a broad range of topics, including family-centred care and cultural capability frameworks, goal-setting, prevention and promotion of communication difficulties in young children, neurodiversity and neurodivergence, and the management of predominant difficulties observed in children under five years of age (e.g., language, literacy, speech, voice, fluency, and feeding).

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 12 (27 Jul - 25 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Weekly on campus tutorials Tutorials will be conducted from weeks 1-8, 10 and 12 of the semester, and will incorporate inquiry-based learning and small group discussion to further explore early speech pathology approaches to the management of communication and feeding/mealtime difficulties in children under five years of age. Tutorials have been designed for experiential learning and therefore, students are expected to attend and participate in all tutorials. It is essential that students prepare for tutorials by completing the online self-paced learning modules and associated preparation activities. As students will be working in small groups during this learning activity, tutorials will not be recorded. Due to the public holiday in Week 3, a make up tutorial activity will be timetabled outside regular tutorial hours. See personal timetable for further details.
Introductory lecture The introductory lecture (week 1) will provide an overview of speech pathology management of communication and feeding/mealtime difficulties in young children.

Fluency Practical In Week 2, students will participate in a paediatric fluency practical session in place of their regular tutorial. This session will use inquiry-based learning and small group discussions to deepen understanding of early speech pathology management for fluency/stuttering difficulties in children under five years old. To make the most of this session, students must complete the online self-paced learning module and related preparation activities beforehand. As this is a small-group, interactive activity, it will not be recorded.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 11 To Week 12
learning_activities.topic: Paediatric Feeding Practical On Monday in Week 11 OR Week 12, students will participate in one 2-hour practical activity focused on paediatric feeding, designed to support the development of skills in managing paediatric dysphagia. During the session, students will complete a series of part tasks (e.g., infant oral reflex examination, positioning, cue reading, and use of feeding equipment) and engage in a simulated interaction with the caregiver of a child experiencing feeding difficulties. Attendance is highly encouraged as this activity will not be recorded.

Supporting neurodivergent children and families workshop In Week 11, an organisation specialised in supporting autistic children and families will deliver a workshop focused on supporting the communication needs of neurodivergent children. The session will provide practical strategies and insights to enhance inclusive and effective communication across clinical and educational settings. Attendance is highly encouraged as this learning activity will not be recorded. Note. This workshop will be timetabled outside regular tutorial hours.

Final lecture The final lecture will be pre-recorded and released in Week 13. This lecture will review the course and provide direction for knowledge translation into later courses and future learning activities in the program.
